author: Priyanka Patel
title: Danny Boyle's 'Extermination' Trilogy Plans
text:
LONDON, June 18, 2025 – Get ready too run: Danny Boyle is back in the director’s chair for a new “ Extermination ” trilogy, starting with “extermination: Evolution,” promising a fresh take on the zombie genre.
The first film, budgeted at $60 million, hits theaters June 30.
Danny Boyle, known for “slumdog Millionaire” and “Trainspotting,” is directing the first installment. The new film explores themes of death, trauma, and the struggle between humanity and primal instincts. “Extermination: Evolution” is set to premiere on June 30. What’s new in the “Extermination” universe? the “Extermination” franchise, which initially revolutionized the zombie genre, is back with a new trilogy, and the first film, “Extermination: Evolution,” is already generating buzz. With a fresh take, this installment promises to be a must-see for horror fans.
Critics are already raving. “extermination: Evolution” has a 95% rating. David Ehrlich of IndieWire praised the film’s approach, calling it a search for salvation within a post-apocalyptic drama. Peter Debruge from Variety notes that the sequel goes deeper, focusing on the fear of dying and the fear of others.
Pro Tip: Re-watching the original “Extermination” film can provide valuable context and heighten your gratitude for the thematic evolution in the new trilogy.
Jodie Eating and Ralph Fiennes in ‘Extermination: Evolution’ (Photo: Next Big Picture) The film, with a budget of $60 million, explores themes far beyond simple gore. Sony, recognizing the potential, secured the rights to film “Extermination: Evolution” and its sequel, “The Bone Temple,” back-to-back. If all goes according to plan, a third film is in the works.
Did You Know? The “Extermination” series was initially inspired by the socio-political climate of the early 2000s, reflecting anxieties about globalization and societal breakdown.
Boyle joked about his plans for the third film. He wants to close his zombie trilogy big. While Boyle directs the first installment, the second is helmed by Nia DaCosta. Boyle said DaCosta did “a great job.”
Danny Boyle,director of ‘Extermination: Evolution’ (Photo: Grantland) The “Extermination” series,from its debut in 2002,has always been more than just a horror franchise. It’s used the zombie genre to explore contemporary anxieties. The new trilogy delves into deeper fears: the denial of death, collective trauma, and the thin line between humanity and the beast. “Extermination: Evolution” opens on June 30 and stars Jodie Comer,Aaron taylor-Johnson,and Ralph Fiennes.
the original “Extermination” films, with their unflinching look at societal collapse, established a precedent for the series’ focus on real-world anxieties. This new trilogy, beginning with “Extermination: Evolution,” appears poised to continue this tradition, but with a deeper exploration of human experience amidst the impending doom of a zombie apocalypse. The series’ longevity and continued relevance speak to its ability to tap into our deepest fears, making audiences see themselves reflected in the horror. The new installment, set to release on June 30, aims to push thes boundaries further.
The Evolution of “Extermination” Themes What distinguishes this new trilogy from previous installments? The shift towards exploring more profound themes is crucial. Where earlier films used the zombie outbreak as a backdrop for social commentary, “Extermination: Evolution” delves into the psychological impact of trauma and the struggle for survival against both external threats and internal demons.
This evolution is evident in the film’s focus, as critics noted.This focus is away from simple gore and toward the core of existential dread.By examining the characters’ mental states, the film offers a more nuanced understanding of human behavior when facing the end of the world, and it does so without losing the action and suspense that the franchise is known for.
The new trilogy uses the zombie genre in a fresh way. “Extermination: Evolution” doesn’t just bring the undead back. It also brings a search for meaning in a world ravaged by chaos. This installment promises to be more than just a horror film; it is also a psychological drama.
“Extermination: evolution” will explore themes of mortality and the blurred lines between humanity and monstrosity. The film challenges us to confront our fears about death and the unknown. Furthermore, the trilogy promises to push the boundaries of the genre thru character-driven storytelling and high-stakes action.
